html:
The Warrwa are an Aboriginal people of the west Kimberley in Western Australia, around King Sound and the lower Fitzroy River near present day Derby.

Their language belongs to the Nyulnyulan family, like that of the Nyikina, their neighbours upriver, and the Nyulnyul on the Dampier Peninsula. To the north were the Umiida and Unggumi.

King Sound has some of the biggest tides in Australia, and Warrwa people knew its mudflats and mangroves well. From the 1880s Derby grew as a port for pastoral stations, and the Warrwa were drawn into station work. Few people speak the language today. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Warrwa are an Aboriginal people of the west Kimberley in Western Australia, around King Sound and the lower Fitzroy River near present day Derby.
